title: Pre-training Antibody Language Models for Antigen-Specific Computational Antibody Design

problem.claim: Computational antibody design must generate complementarity-determining regions that determine antibody specificity and binding affinity.

gap.claim: Existing computational methods rely heavily on limited high-quality antibody structure data, while CDRs are highly variable and difficult to predict.

contributions.claim: Develops an antibody pre-training language model based on antibody sequence data.
Proposes one-shot sequence and structure generation for CDRs to address costs and error propagation associated with autoregressive methods.
Integrates the pre-trained antibody model into an antigen-specific antibody generation model with designed modules.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their antibody language model as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their method outperforms previous baselines on sequence and structure generation, CDR-H3 design for antigen binding, and antibody optimization.
The authors report that code is available in the linked GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Antibodies protect the human body by binding to pathogens, and deep learning has attracted attention for computational antibody design.
Structure-data scarcity and CDR variability make CDR generation difficult.
Abundant antibody sequence data may help model CDRs and reduce reliance on structure data.
The paper pre-trains an antibody language model, uses one-shot CDR sequence and structure generation, and incorporates the model into antigen-specific antibody generation.
The authors report superiority over previous baselines across several generation, design, and optimization tasks.

source_observation.claim: Large antibody sequence datasets are used to reduce reliance on scarce high-quality structure data.

interpretation.claim: Sequence-based pre-training can provide a way to mitigate structural-data scarcity in antibody design.

application.claim: When labeled or structural data are limited, pre-train on more abundant sequence data before applying the model to structure-aware design tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that sequence pre-training is sufficient without structure data or that the approach generalizes beyond the reported antibody tasks.

source_observation.claim: The method uses one-shot CDR sequence and structure generation to mitigate costs and error propagation associated with autoregressive methods.

interpretation.claim: Reducing sequential generation dependencies may lower computational cost and accumulated generation errors.

application.claim: For coupled sequence-and-structure generation, consider non-autoregressive or one-shot generation when sequential error propagation is a material concern.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the trade-offs, constraints, or conditions under which one-shot generation is preferable.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset sizes, data splits, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not identify the previous baselines or quantify performance differences.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture or carefully designed modules in detail.
The abstract does not provide experimental conditions, ablations, or limitations.
